prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: The change to your flight schedules page has made it unprintable - I relied heavily on printable schedules for my VP.
Delta: Hello, Kenny. Sorry to hear. We will look into this. We appreciate your feedback.  *ARD

Customer: Thanks for booking my dog on a flight that does not exists after confirming the booking and reverifying yesterday when I called everything was good to go  :-(.......
Delta: Oh no! What flight number was your dog booked on and between which cities? *ASK

Customer: EVERY time I fly  something always goes wrong.
Delta: Hello Olivia, I am so sorry is there anything I can help with? Thank you.   *TJM

Customer: unable to add API for our NYC trip message check in 24hours before is this correct?
Delta: Hi Lynne. Please DM your confirmation number, and I'll do my best to help. Thanks! *TMS https://t.co/6iDGBJAc2m

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: website_app_issue):
"""I try to change my booking, but it seems that your website has a bud. On every page, it displays the correct flight with the correct dates, but the system shows a wrong connecting time. What should I do? I am worried that I end up booking a wrong flight"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: Hi there, sorry for the trouble. Please DM us your confirmation number and the itinerary details so we can look into the connecting time issue. Thank you.
